title: Service Promises: cross-team experiment plan for SLO adoption and error-budget learning
content:
Purpose
This doc proposes a lightweight cross-functional experiment to teach teams how to define pragmatic service promises (SLOs), run short error-budget experiments, and make operational decisions from the outcome. Goal is capability-building + producing 3 service-level contracts we can reuse as templates. Not a company-wide rollout plan — this is intentionally scoped as a 10-week learning cadence.

Why this approach
- We repeatedly see either: (a) teams set unrealistic 99.999 targets that are unimplemented, or (b) no targets exist and teams rely on page/noise.
- Focus on hands-on experiments instead of long docs: run, measure, iterate.
- Produce artifacts: service promise template, measurement dashboard, incident decision rubric, and a short how-to note for feature teams.

Objectives (measurable)
1) Ship 3 validated service promises (SLO + error budget policy + simple dashboard) for representative services by end of experiment.
2) Train 6 engineers/PMs across 3 feature teams to author and operate an SLO in production.
3) Reduce noisy pages for participating services by 30% during the 4 weeks after policy activation (baseline measured by oncall paging rate).

Scope
In-scope: public HTTP inference API (small endpoints), embedding pipeline consumer, web UI session service.
Out-of-scope: infra-level device drivers, batch training jobs, 3rd-party vendor availability (we will capture vendor SLAs but not enforce).

Experiment design (10 weeks)
Phase A — Discover (Weeks 1–2)
- Kickoff workshop (2 hours) with SRE, product, infra, and the 3 selected feature teams. Objective: align on user journeys and critical requests.
- Quick telemetry scan: determine current P50/P95/P99 latency, error rates, and paging triggers for each candidate service (owners: Arjun + Claire).
- Deliverable: One-page service brief per candidate with current signal map.

Phase B — Hypothesis & Policy (Weeks 3–4)
- For each service, propose 1 SLO (type, target, measurement window) + an error-budget policy (what happens on burn). Example candidates: 99.9% successful-requests over 7d for embedding pipeline; 99.5% session-availability over 1d for web UI.
- Quick prioritization rubric: customer impact, traffic volume, observability readiness.
- Deliverable: SLO proposal doc + owner signoff (product + SRE).

Phase C — Canary & Experiment (Weeks 5–8)
- Implement minimal instrumentation to measure SLO (prometheus metrics, labels, or route-level counting). If missing, add proxy-layer counters rather than deep code changes.
- Create a lightweight dashboard in Console: per-service SLO view + recent burn incidents (owner: Miguel).
- Run error-budget experiments: intentionally throttle non-critical requests, or enable a cost-saving config, to observe how burn manifests and how runbooks behave. Keep experiments reversible and low blast radius.
- Track pages and noise.

Phase D — Learn & Embed (Weeks 9–10)
- Retrospective with each team: what worked, where metrics lied, changes to runbook.
- Finalize service promise templates and publish short how-to note.
- Capture follow-ups (operational automation, external vendor alignment) into product backlog.

Metrics and signals to monitor
- Primary SLO signal (success_count / total_count) with rolling window as defined per service.
- Error budget remaining (percent) and sustained burn rate.
- Oncall paging rate (pages/week) and mean time to acknowledge.
- Customer-visible latency percentiles (P95) for the same window as the SLO.
- False-positive alerts (alerts that did not correspond to actionable degradation).

Roles & responsibilities (working RACI-lite)
- SRE lead (Sofia): experiment owner, run kickoff, help design measurement, host retros.
- Instrumentation engineer (Arjun): implement metrics, advise on dashboards.
- Product reps (one per team): declare user journeys and decide acceptable tradeoffs.
- Feature team owners (Claire, Miguel, Leah): implement minimal counters, test runbooks, iterate.
- Observability platform (shared): host dashboards and store historical burn.

Decision rules & error-budget actions
- Minor burn (>= 10% but < 30% of budget over 24h): restrict non-critical background work, increase alert thresholds, and run a 48h mitigation sprint.
- Major burn (>= 30% over 24h or 100% total): escalate to SRE lead + product; enable emergency rollback or degradations; open incident channel.
- If repeated major burns across two weekly windows, convert the service promise to an engineering improvement ticket with target SLA changes.

Communication plan
- Weekly status note to #reliability-ops (short summary + links to dashboards).
- Mid-experiment show-and-tell (15min) in the Engineering All-Hands.
- Final deliverable: short Confluence recipe + link to dashboard and runbooks.

Risks and mitigations
- Poor instrumentation: mitigate by proxy counting and a short instrumentation guardrail checklist.
- Team bandwidth: prioritize minimal code changes and use feature flags for canaries.
- Overly aggressive SLO targets: use hypothesis iteration and keep targets conservative for first 3 services.

Deliverables
- 3 signed service promise packages (SLO spec, dashboard, runbook).
- Instrumentation cookbook for lightweight SLO measurement.
- Short post-mortem template for experiments.
- Confluence recipe and a short recording of the kickoff workshop.

Timeline (high level)
Week 1: Kickoff + telemetry scans
Week 2: Service briefs
Week 3: SLO proposals
Week 4: Owner signoffs
Week 5–7: Instrument + dashboard + canaries
Week 8: Experiment completion + data collection
Week 9: Team retros + finalize artifacts
Week 10: Publish recipes + handoff backlog

Quick checklist (first run)
- [ ] Confirm participating teams and product reps
- [ ] Baseline telemetry exported to common dashboard
- [ ] Draft SLO proposals for each service
- [ ] Minimal counters instrumented and validated
- [ ] Error-budget experiment plan approved by SRE lead
- [ ] Retrospective scheduled

Outstanding questions (to resolve in kickoff)
- Which user journeys are truly critical vs nice-to-have? Need product prioritization input.
- Are there any regulatory/enterprise customers that need tighter windows? Who to notify?
- Slack escalation flow — should we use a separate channel per experiment?

Notes & references
- See linked Confluence recipe after experiment (confluence:DEP-487-service-contracts).
- Instrumentation primer: github:pull/4532 (work-in-progress).
- Current implementation tickets: jira:ENG-1729, jira:ENG-1782 (dashboard plumbing).

Summary
This plan trades breadth for depth: run a repeatable, low-blast experiment with three representative services, deliver practical artifacts, and upskill product + engineering on authoring and operating service promises. The goal is not perfection — it is to create a replicable learning pattern that scales across teams.
